mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising the cost of capital and depressing corporate earnings growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% is associated with weakening household demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month stretches of INDPRO contraction exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 6% combined with a federal funds rate below 2% for three months signals a delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which raises uncertainty and volatility, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate eventual policy normalization.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes where CPIAUCSL exceeds 6% and FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 300k month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows by more than 300k for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over a 5-day horizon; when RSAFS rises month-over-month, consumer discretionary stocks outperform, lifting the index in the very short term.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
